charts.title: Consolidated Revenue vs BMW JV Share vs Net Income

charts.annotation: Profit incl. NCI is total group profit before splitting out non-controlling interests; the gap to attributable Net Income is the minority share.

charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Brilliance China Automotive Holdings Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Brilliance China Automotive Holdings Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Brilliance China Automotive Holdings Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Brilliance China Automotive Holdings Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Brilliance China Automotive Holdings Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Brilliance China Automotive Holdings Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is from consolidated operations; net income is attributable to owners; profit incl. NCI adds back the non-controlling-interest slice before the attributable split.

For Brilliance China Automotive Holdings Limited: gross profit comes almost entirely from the small consolidated manufacturing business, while net income is dominated by the equity-accounted BMW Brilliance JV result below — see the JV chart above for the magnitude gap between the two.

What to watch:

  • Net income tracking the JV chart, not consolidated gross profit
  • Profit incl. NCI diverging from attributable net income (minority stakes in consolidated subsidiaries)

jvShare.title: BMW JV share vs consolidated revenue
jvShare.content:
Brilliance China owns 25% of BMW Brilliance Automotive, the BMW-badged manufacturing JV in China, accounted for under the equity method. Its result is reported as share of associates and JV results and sits almost entirely outside consolidated revenue, which instead reflects the much smaller parts/components businesses this holding company fully consolidates.

For Brilliance China Automotive Holdings Limited: consolidated revenue has run roughly RMB1-4bn a year while the JV share alone has reached RMB14bn (FY2021) — net income tracks the JV line, not revenue, so revenue growth or decline is a poor proxy for the investment case here.

What to watch:

  • JV share trend (BMW China volumes, pricing, EV transition, royalty/model-mix with Brilliance)
  • Dividends actually upstreamed from the JV versus the equity-accounted result (cash conversion)
  • Any change in Brilliance's 25% stake or BMW's consolidation terms

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Brilliance China Automotive Holdings Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Brilliance China Automotive Holdings Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
